title: Vicky Kaushal Has Disappeared — and He Won't Be Back for 18 Months
excerpt: The actor has locked himself into an unprecedented year-and-a-half commitment to play the immortal warrior Parashurama in Amar Kaushik's mythological epic Mahavatar — no other films, no distractions, just transformation.
body:
Somewhere in Mumbai right now, Vicky Kaushal is not on a film set. He's not on a red carpet. He's not promoting anything. He is, by all credible accounts, locked inside a training facility, reshaping his body and rewiring his instincts for a role that will consume the next eighteen months of his life.

The role is Chiranjeevi Parashurama — the axe-wielding immortal warrior-sage of Hindu mythology — in Mahavatar, directed by Amar Kaushik (of *Stree* and *Bhediya* fame) and produced by Maddock Films. And the commitment Vicky has made to this project is unlike anything a mainstream Bollywood actor has attempted in recent memory.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=U5FlDDj7AP0

Eighteen months. No other films. No brand shoots. No "quick projects on the side." Just Parashurama.

The Timeline: From Bhansali's Set to the Gym

The story begins with Sanjay Leela Bhansali's *Love and War*, which co-stars Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt. Bhansali has been racing through a 50-day schedule that began in May 2026, aiming to wrap by the end of June for a theatrical release on January 21, 2027. The moment Vicky steps off Bhansali's set, he steps into Amar Kaushik's world.

The first six months — June through December 2026 — are pure preparation. According to an exclusive *Pinkvilla* report, the prep module includes a rigorous physical transformation (bulking up to match the mythological scale of the character), intensive acting workshops, and what sources describe as deep psychological immersion into Parashurama's emotional arc.

> "Amar has designed a very detailed prep module for Vicky. It's not just about the physicality, but also about getting into the psychological and emotional graph of the character." — Industry source to Pinkvilla

Principal photography is slated for January 2027, running a full year through December 2027. During this time, Vicky will not take on any other project — a decision that, in an industry where top stars routinely juggle three or four films simultaneously, feels almost radical.

> "Vicky is treating Mahavatar as a once-in-a-lifetime project. He wants to be fully invested, which is why he has consciously decided not to take up any other assignments during the shoot." — Source close to the production

Why This Role Could Define a Career

Vicky Kaushal has already proven he can carry a film on his shoulders. *Uri: The Surgical Strike* turned him into a household name. *Sardar Udham* showed he could disappear into historical gravity. *Sam Bahadur* gave him command. And *Chhaava*, his last release in 2025, demonstrated he could handle period armour and battlefield choreography with conviction.

But Parashurama is different. This isn't a real historical figure with documented photographs and newsreel footage. This is a mythological immortal — one of the seven Chiranjeevis — a being of immense spiritual depth and terrifying physical power, wielding a divine axe granted by Lord Shiva himself. The first-look posters, unveiled on Parashuram Jayanti, showed Vicky in long hair, a thick beard, and surrounded by fire. He looked magnificent and barely recognisable.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZHiw5gCOCp/

The character demands something actors rarely get to attempt: building a physical and emotional vocabulary from mythology rather than biography. How does an immortal warrior move? What does centuries of rage and penance look like in someone's eyes? These are the questions Amar Kaushik's workshops are designed to answer.

The Bigger Picture: Bollywood's Mythology Arms Race

Vicky's Mahavatar doesn't exist in a vacuum. Rajamouli is building his Varanasi-set mythology epic with Mahesh Babu. Ranbir Kapoor leads Ramayana, headed to Comic-Con this July with a Hans Zimmer–AR Rahman score. Ranveer Singh just committed to the ₹300-crore zombie survival epic Pralay. The biggest male stars in Indian cinema are all betting on scale, spectacle, and long production timelines — a clear pivot away from quick commercial turnarounds.

For the diaspora audience watching from New York, London, and Toronto, this matters. These are the films designed to play globally — in IMAX, in Dolby, in languages and markets that Bollywood has historically struggled to crack. Mahavatar, with its mythological foundation and pan-India ambitions, is positioned to be exactly that kind of event.

What Katrina Kaif Thinks (We Don't Know, But We Can Guess)

Here's the domestic subplot nobody's reporting: Katrina Kaif and Vicky are parents to a young son, Vihaan, born in 2025. An eighteen-month disappearance into a single character means extended shoots, gruelling physical schedules, and the kind of single-minded focus that doesn't always play well with bedtime routines. Katrina, who took a deliberate step back from the spotlight after Vihaan's birth, has reportedly been supportive of Vicky's ambitions — her May 2026 Instagram recap featured tender moments with both Vicky and their son, suggesting a couple navigating this phase together rather than apart.

The Wait

Mahavatar is expected to arrive in theatres in 2028 — likely as a grand pan-India release across languages. Between now and then, Vicky Kaushal will essentially vanish from the Bollywood circuit. No gossip columns. No promotional rounds. Just a man turning himself into a god.

If this works — if the film delivers on even half of its mythological ambition — it won't just be the role that defines Vicky Kaushal's career. It'll be the role that proves Bollywood can make mythology feel as alive as Marvel made comic books feel.

For now, the axe is being sharpened. The rest of us just have to wait.
